artifacts.summary: Five-phase, four-wave plan relocating the --meta/--review/--dream sub-modes from memory's /distill into a new core-owned /telemetry command and skill-telemetry skill, re-anchoring six previously undiscovered dependencies and repointing every cross-extension citation.

user_decision.question: The three relocated sub-modes need a core-owned host command, since memory's /distill command file stays in the extension being retired. The plan picks the command's name; the sub-mode flag names and specifications are unchanged either way.
options: /telemetry --meta|--review|--dream -- one new core command hosting all three flags under their existing names
A different command name of your choosing (e.g. /signal or /reflect) hosting the same three flags
Fold --meta onto the existing /meta command and host only --review/--dream elsewhere
user_decision.recommended: /telemetry --meta|--review|--dream -- one new core command hosting all three flags under their existing names

memory_candidates.content: Relocating prose from an extension's context tree into agent-system/extensions/core/** is never a verbatim copy: core/** is a deliverable tree where rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md and rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md both apply and are enforced at write time by hooks/validate-no-record-versioning.sh and hooks/validate-no-task-references.sh. Extension-local specifications routinely narrate their own draft history ('redefined by X, not deletion', 'inherits in substance unchanged from the current Y section', 'Phase N removes the now-duplicated copy', 'pre-redefinition, historical') because their origin tree was never linted for it. Plan a de-narration pass as an explicit task in the phase that lands the copy, or the write is rejected mid-phase.
